title: Edge-case token cost vs perf-per-watt sweep (A10, L4, A100, H100)
summary: Compact sweep comparing $/token and tokens-per-joule across A10, L4, A100, H100 under a small-sequence interactive workload. Highlights tradeoffs where cheapest $/token does not align with best perf/W and calls out region & sustained-throughput caveats.
assumptions: Model proxy: 13B decoder-only inference v1 (int8), synthetic prompts; seq_len=64 generation token (single-token steady-state); continuous batching enabled; measurement window 30 minutes. Hourly instance costs (spot-like): A10=$0.48, L4=$0.95, A100=$2.20, H100=$3.60. Grid power price assumption $0.12/kWh only for energy-dollar sensitivity (not applied to $/token shown). Power draw is measured GPU board-level avg while serving (excl. host idle): A10=150W, L4=110W, A100=400W, H100=450W. Results are per-GPU, single-worker baseline (no multi-GPU model parallelization).

recommendations:
1) If target is raw $/token for lightweight 13B-class models with small seqs, prioritize A10 - cheapest in this sweep provided latency constraints are moderate.
2) For energy-sensitive or on-prem sites with carbon/utility constraints, L4 provides the best tokens-per-joule and should be considered first for sustained workloads.
3) Use A100 when you need balance of latency and per-token cost under medium-to-high concurrency; consider multi-GPU sharding for >1k tokens/sec sustained.
4) H100 reserved for latency-critical, high-batch throughput scenarios; evaluate whether batch consolidation + model parallelism reduces effective $/token before picking H100.
5) Add a second measurement sweep at seq_len=512 and with mixed-precision/residual quantization (int4 where possible) — the relative ordering can flip for longer contexts.
6) Incorporate regional hourly price variance (±30%) and sustained-use discounts into the cost model; store baseline numbers as constants so we can re-run sensitivity automatically.
notes:
Why this is different: focuses expressly on the divergence between dollars-per-token and energy efficiency (tokens-per-joule) for interactive, steady-state small-seq workloads. Contains compact CSV-style table for easy import into ad-hoc sheets/analysis.
Measurement caveats: burst vs sustained power draw differs; host CPU/IO and NVMe hot caching can add 20-40W depending on image I/O patterns; network egress not included.
Open questions: how does continuous KV cache hit rate alter effective $/token for chat workloads? Add sample workload traces from prod to re-weight the token mix (prefix vs generation).
